decisionBasis.requiredConsistency: A tested output intervention lowers dimmed-response-mask MAE against matched WebGL by more than repeat-capture noise plus 0.5 RGB levels in every priority state.
decisionBasis.interpretation: At least one isolated output-stage intervention contributes consistently to the dimmed-region discrepancy, while the measured residual remains much larger than repeat noise. This does not establish a complete cause or authorize a correction/promotion.

promotionBoundary: Anatomy remains M2 — OPT-IN IMPLEMENTATION INCOMPLETE.

provenance.workingTreeStatusExplanation: The only porcelain status item was the environment-provided node_modules symlink to the primary checkout; the measured source revision is the committed measurementCommit.

priorBaselineReference.purpose: Full 13-state PR #262 matched WebGL, native standard WebGPU, and native material-aware baseline. The native-required 13-state audit passed in this task (2 passed, 1 expected skip).

interventionMatrix.B1: Bypass custom per-material RGB tone-map and display-color conversion for dimmed targets only.
interventionMatrix.B2: Bypass tone mapping for dimmed targets while retaining sRGB conversion.
interventionMatrix.B3: Bypass sRGB conversion for dimmed targets while retaining authored tone-mapping behavior.
interventionMatrix.B4: Bypass custom per-material RGB output transform for highlighted targets only.

visibilityPolicies.C1: Keep 1 explicitly identified dimmed renderable(s) visible; exclude the rest of the current dimmed group. Keep every non-dimmed renderable at baseline visibility.
visibilityPolicies.C2: Keep 2 explicitly identified dimmed renderable(s) visible; exclude the rest of the current dimmed group. Keep every non-dimmed renderable at baseline visibility.
visibilityPolicies.C4: Exclude every currently visible dimmed semantic camera renderable; keep highlighted, normal, registered-target, overlay, and other renderables at their baseline visibility.
visibilityPolicies.C3: Full current dimmed group remains visible with every other renderable at baseline visibility.

masks.method: Within-renderer B0 framebuffer differences from excluding current presentation-group renderable IDs, with an RGB per-channel threshold of 8.
masks.limitation: Masks are observed visibility responses, not exact silhouettes or additive color decomposition. The complement is an unaffected/background candidate.
masks.bothGroupIntersectionMeaning: A non-empty intersection means pixels changed when either group was excluded; it does not prove simultaneous visible-surface overlap.

targetSelection.source: Mounted ConceptualCameraAnatomyPresentation resolved with the same resolveConceptualAnatomyPartState contract and joined to current visible renderable UUIDs.

visibilityRestoration.interpretation: Observed visibility-response masks include occlusion, reveal, depth, blending and shadow effects; the unaffected complement is a background/unaffected candidate, not an exact semantic decomposition.

pairwiseB1.interpretation: Intersection of actual per-part visibility-exclusion response masks. This demonstrates that both tested part sets influence some measured output pixels; it is not an exact silhouette or an additive alpha decomposition.

shaderActivationEvidence.reasonPerCopyGraphCountMayBeZero: Three may reuse the already compiled B1 program for a scoped copy with the same material family and output-transform cache key; the experiment therefore checks B1 graph activation in the same state, the pair's actual output-copy identity/version, and repeated framebuffer captures.

pairwiseNonAdditivity.interpretation: The residual compares simultaneous B1 output change against the sum of each part's separate B1 output change in the measured shared-response mask. It is evidence of non-additive framebuffer response under this setup, not a direct alpha-blending diagnosis.

remainingUnknowns: The screenshot is a browser-composited canvas capture; unchanged screenshot alpha does not qualify renderer-context premultiplication.
A pixel-mask intersection records common measured response, not exact transparent surface overlap or additive layer contribution.
Hardware acceleration is unconfirmed; native WebGPU execution is qualified by the mounted renderer family/backend and no-fallback evidence.
recommendation: Keep Anatomy M2. A later, separately reviewed proposal may test a narrow color-space/output-stage correction, but first measure the remaining dimmed error with a GPU blend-intermediate capture for the qualifying single-part and two-part visibility conditions. Do not start PR N from this evidence alone.
